hook.situation: You are texting someone what you are doing right now, why you did not reply, or what happened during another action.
objectives: Use V-고 있어요 for an action in progress.
Use V-는 중이에요 or N 중이에요 when you are right in the middle of something.
Use V-는 동안 to show what happens during the same time span.
hook.whyItMatters: Korean does not need a separate word like English 'am/is/are doing.' The ongoing meaning is built with endings and nouns: 공부하고 있어요, 공부하는 중이에요, 공부하는 동안. These forms make Kakao replies and daily updates much more natural.

grammarNotes.title: V-고 있다 - action in progress
grammarNotes.mentalModel: V-고 있어요 puts the camera on an action that is currently happening or continuing around now.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -고 있다 to the verb stem: 먹다 becomes 먹고 있어요, 공부하다 becomes 공부하고 있어요, 기다리다 becomes 기다리고 있어요. Past progressive uses -고 있었어요. Do not use it with plain adjectives like 바쁘다 or 피곤하다.

examples.en: I am studying Korean at the library.

examples.ko: 지금 전화하고 있어서 메시지를 못 봤어요.
examples.romanization: jigeum jeonhwahago isseoseo mesijireul mot bwasseoyo.
examples.en: I was on a call, so I did not see the message.
examples.note: The ongoing action explains why the reply was delayed.

examples.en: I am learning exercise these days.
examples.note: -고 있어요 can also describe an ongoing life activity around this period.

contrastPairs.explanation: The plain present can mean habit or general action. -고 있어요 focuses on progress.
Past tense reports completion. -고 있었어요 says the action was in progress at that time.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Do not attach -고 있어요 to adjectives. If you mean a current activity, use an action verb like 일하다.

exceptions: Some verbs with -고 있다 can describe a resulting state: 옷을 입고 있어요 means 'I am wearing clothes.'
In casual speech, 하고 있어요 often shortens to 하고 있어요 / 하고 있어, but the structure stays the same.
For a very immediate 'in the middle of' feeling, V-는 중이에요 can sound more precise.

grammarNotes.title: V-는 중이에요 / N 중이에요 - in the middle of
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 중 means middle. V-는 중이에요 says you are inside the action right now.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -는 중이에요 to an action verb: 먹는 중이에요, 기다리는 중이에요, 만드는 중이에요. ㄹ-stems drop ㄹ before 는: 만들다 becomes 만드는 중이에요. With a noun, use N 중이에요: 회의 중이에요, 수업 중이에요, 전화 중이에요.

examples.en: I am in the middle of waiting for a friend.
examples.note: The waiting is happening right now.

examples.en: I am still in a meeting.
examples.note: Noun plus 중 is compact and common in messages.

examples.en: I am on my way right now.
examples.note: A very common reply when someone asks where you are.

b.en: I am in the middle of studying.

contrastPairs.explanation: -고 있어요 is broad ongoing action. -는 중이에요 zooms in on the current task.
Both work. N 중이에요 is shorter and very natural as a status reply.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: With verbs, use the modifier form before 중. The dictionary form cannot attach directly.

exceptions: Do not use -는 중 with adjectives: 피곤한 중이에요 is unnatural.
N 중 can appear without 이에요 in signs: 공사 중, 수업 중, 통화 중.
가는 중이에요 often means 'on my way,' not simply 'I am going' in a broad sense.

grammarNotes.title: V-는 동안 - while / during
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 동안 draws a time box. One action happens inside the time span of another action.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -는 동안 to an action verb: 기다리는 동안, 공부하는 동안, 자는 동안. With a time noun, place the noun before 동안: 한 시간 동안, 방학 동안. Use 동안 for the whole span, not just a single moment.

examples.en: I could not see the message during the meeting.
examples.note: The meeting is the span when another thing did not happen.

examples.en: I read a book while waiting.
While studying, I do not look at my phone.
examples.note: A rule that applies throughout the study span.
A duration noun can come before 동안.

a.en: Do not call when I sleep.

b.en: A call came while I was sleeping.

contrastPairs.explanation: 때 points to the occasion. 동안 stresses the whole span.

a.en: I listen to music while studying.

b.en: I study, but I also listen to music.

contrastPairs.explanation: 동안 is time overlap. It does not express contrast.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Use the present modifier -는 before 동안 for action verbs.

exceptions: 동안 is not the contrastive English 'while.' For contrast, use -지만 or -는데.
With nouns of duration, no verb modifier is needed: 방학 동안, 세 시간 동안.
For a moment rather than a span, use 때.

readingText.title: Why the reply was late
readingText.body: 지훈은 도서관에서 한국어를 공부하고 있었어요. 민서가 메시지를 보냈지만 지훈은 바로 답장하지 못했어요. 그때 지훈은 회의하는 동안 휴대폰을 보지 못했고, 회의가 끝난 뒤에도 발표 자료를 만드는 중이었어요. 민서는 카페에서 친구를 기다리는 중이라 시간이 조금 있었어요. 그래서 두 사람은 지훈이 끝나면 잠깐 전화하기로 했어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Jihoon was studying Korean at the library. Minseo sent a message, but Jihoon could not reply right away. During the meeting he could not check his phone, and after the meeting he was still making presentation materials. Minseo had a little time because she was waiting for a friend at a cafe, so they decided to call briefly when Jihoon finished.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 지훈은 왜 메시지를 바로 못 봤어요?

culturalNote.title: Short status replies
culturalNote.body: In Korean messaging, short status replies like 회의 중이에요, 가는 중이에요, and 지금 공부하고 있어요 are common and polite. They explain availability without over-explaining.
culturalNote.tip: Use N 중이에요 for quick status, and V-고 있어요 when you want to state the actual action.

Which sentence is the best short status reply?
inlineExercises.explanation: N 중이에요 is a compact way to say an activity is in progress.

inlineExercises.prompt: During the meeting, I could not see the message.
inlineExercises.explanation: -는 동안 gives the time span during another action.
Use the verb modifier -는 before 중: 기다리는 중이에요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the sentence: 저는 바쁘고 있어요.
inlineExercises.explanation: Do not attach -고 있어요 to adjectives. Use a direct adjective or an action verb.

bullets: V-고 있어요 marks an action in progress: 한국어를 공부하고 있어요.
V-는 중이에요 and N 중이에요 focus on being in the middle of something: 회의 중이에요.
V-는 동안 marks an overlapping time span: 회의하는 동안 메시지를 못 봤어요.
Do not use -고 있어요 with adjectives like 바쁘다 or 피곤하다.
